safety_lead_time.comparison_action: increase from SAP value of 0.0 days to 2.48 days

narrative: Material PL3__M06DA03F shows intermittent, high-variability demand (CV=1.80) with only 27.8% of working days carrying positive demand, averaging 2.12 units/day. Lead times are very short (mean 0.70 days) and stable (CV=0.17), limiting exposure to supply risk. The current SAP policy carries zero safety stock, leaving the material unprotected against demand spikes. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with safety stock of 6 units and MOQ-constrained order quantity of 419 achieves 95% service level for a marginal annual cost increase of ~$10.
warnings: Intermittent demand pattern detected (only 27.8% of days have demand)
Current SAP safety stock is 0 - no buffer against uncertainty
Very high demand variability (CV=1.80) - consider review-based policies

research_insights.selection_rationale: Given a very short and stable lead time, a continuous-review (r,Q) policy is appropriate. The MOQ of 419 units dominates the EOQ of 215, making fixed-order-quantity replenishment natural. The intermittent demand pattern does not warrant Croston methods given the brevity of the lead time exposure window.
research_insights.boundary_risk: MOQ (419) + safety stock (6) = 425 units, well within max_storage_units of 1222. No capacity constraint binds. EOQ falls below MOQ, so order frequency is lower than economically optimal — this inflates holding costs slightly but is unavoidable given the supplier minimum.
